title: The Spell Crafter must initiate a retrospective even when there is nothing to discuss
content:
A.1.10.2.4.13.6.1 requires the Spell Crafter to open a retrospective in the existing Spell thread, "prefac[ing] the message with `initiating retro`," including "any problems identified during the Spell, including concrete improvement proposals" — and then: "**If there is nothing to discuss, the Spell Crafter should communicate that** (e.g. `Initiating retro: nothing to discuss from my side`)."

Mandating the null response is the interesting part. Without it, an absent retro is ambiguous between "the cycle was clean" and "nobody got round to it," and those are very different facts about a process. With it, every Spell produces a record, and a missing record is unambiguously a missed step.

The fixed prefix does related work: it makes retros mechanically findable in a busy Slack channel, so "was a retro held for the 2026-03-12 Spell?" is a search rather than an investigation. Cheap searchability is what allows the requirement to be audited at all.

There is also a behavioural effect. Writing "nothing to discuss from my side" is a small act of attribution — it puts a name on the claim that this cycle was clean. That is a slightly higher bar than saying nothing, and it is the moment where a Crafter is most likely to recall the minor annoyance they had otherwise decided not to mention.

The pattern generalizes: where the absence of a signal is indistinguishable from the absence of effort, require the signal to be sent explicitly. The Executive Sheet's "Unconfirmed" default (A.1.10.2.4.2.3.1) applies the same idea to state rather than to communication.
description: A.1.10.2.4.13.6.1 requires an explicit null result prefixed 'initiating retro', so silence can never be mistaken for a clean cycle or for an omitted step.
